resources.string: FireFly 0.1.0. Reticulum and LXMF by Mark Qvist, running unmodified. Same engine as FireFly on RK3326 handhelds. MIT licence.
Stump nodes keep you reachable by DM for an hour after your last announce. Keep this under 60.
Delete everything and ignore them from now on.
Everything with them is deleted, and from now on their messages and announces are ignored on this phone, even if they keep transmitting. You can unblock them in Settings.

Blocking needs only the address: it works even for someone you\'ll never hear again. Unblocked people come back only if they announce or write. Stump room nicknames aren\'t covered: they\'re relayed by the node.
Bluetooth is off, or permission was not granted.

The whole conversation with %1$s is deleted from this phone: messages, voice notes and the contact itself. Anything still being sent is cancelled. They can still write to you, which starts a new conversation.
Delete everything with them. They come back if they announce or write.
If someone is unreachable, leave it on a propagation node
They\'re removed from this phone. If they announce themselves again, they reappear here.
That file is not a Reticulum identity.
Your key is your address. Whoever has it is you on the network; if it is lost, so is your address. Back it up and keep the copy private. Restoring takes effect after Quit and reopen.
Identity %1$s saved. Quit and reopen FireFly to use it.
Join the node\'s Wi-Fi first. Same rooms and identity as over LoRa.
Keep the phone awake while a radio is attached
No conversations yet. People appear here as their announces are heard.
This node keeps messages for people who are offline.
No radio attached: settings apply when one connects.
Applying your settings… on air until then: %1$s
%1$d bytes: needs a link, more airtime
Paired. FireFly connects to it now.
Turn Bluetooth on in the RNode (rnodeconf <port> -b), put it in pairing mode (hold its button, or rnodeconf <port> -p), then tap it below and enter the PIN shown on its screen.
Pairing: enter the PIN shown on the RNode.
Uses the node of the Stump you chat through, or else the nearest one heard.
A propagation node address is 32 hex characters.
Use a node by its address
Messages for people who are offline are left here, and yours are collected from here. Everyone near a Stump should use the same node: they don\'t share messages with each other yet.
None heard yet. FireFly asks every Stump it hears for its node.
Nothing is left for offline people, and nothing is collected.
A propagation node holds messages for people who are offline. It can\'t read them.
Applying your settings to the RNode…
Check the values: 137–1020 MHz, SF 5–12, CR 5–8, 0–22 dBm.
Every node on a mesh must use the same settings. A mismatched radio shows no error; it just hears nothing.
Say something to join the room. Until then the node only sends you private messages.
Saved · your new name is announced
Saved · the radio retunes in a moment
Fill in the Stump defaults (915.0 MHz · 125 kHz · SF8 · 4/5 · 7 dBm)
Off the list, history kept. It comes back if it messages you.
Its rooms, private messages and history are deleted from this phone. This can\'t be undone. If it\'s still on the air, it can appear again later as a new, empty entry.
Delete it and all its history from this phone.
Stump nodes: rooms, people and private messages shared by everyone near a node, and by everyone reachable over LoRa.
Each TCP peer is host:port, one per line.
Hold the button while you speak, release to send.
Voice notes need the microphone permission.
The microphone is busy or unavailable.
Standard: robotic but clear. The default.
Noticeably clearer, twice the airtime of standard.
The best Codec 2 gets, almost three times the airtime of standard.
Smallest: muffled, but the longest notes per packet.
Natural voice (Opus) when your link to the person isn\'t LoRa; Codec 2 1200 when it is. Saves airtime.
%1$s s of speech per LoRa packet · a 15 s note is %2$s KB
Applies to every note you send, voice DMs through a Stump included. Notes you receive play in any quality.
Natural voice on every link. The default. About six times the size of Codec 2 1200: on LoRa a full 15 s note takes about a minute of airtime.
Opus 8 kbps · a 15 s note is about 13.4 KB
● %1$s s / 15 s · slide left to cancel
Announced to everyone. Stump nodes use it as your nick.
This node\'s billboard, for anyone who walks up. Posts disappear 72 hours after they\'re made.
Posted. It\'s on the board for 72 hours.
The node didn\'t keep this post. Try again.
This node no longer offers a billboard.
Files people brought to this node. Bringing one earns credits; taking one spends them.
Files people brought to this node. Take what you like, and bring something back.
There\'s no SD card in the node right now, so there\'s nothing to share.
Leave a file on this node for others.
If someone set a slot aside for you on this node, enter its code. Otherwise leave this empty.
it\'s not on the shelf any more
no SD card in the node
the Wi-Fi connection to the node was lost
Can\'t reach the node over Wi-Fi. Are you on its network?
The node answered with an error (%1$d).
The node couldn\'t save the post (its card may be full).
%1$s is on the shelf. Your balance: %2$d
%1$s was delivered to the slot set aside for you.
Downloaded. Tap Install; Android asks once to let FireFly install apps.
installs over this one only if it\'s signed with the same key
Wi-Fi, this network and LoRa, best link first
The phone isn\'t on Wi-Fi. Scan for a Stump\'s hotspot below, or join one in Android\'s Wi-Fi settings.
No Stump answers at %1$s, this Wi-Fi\'s gateway. This is probably an ordinary router: search this network below.
Each Stump runs its own Wi-Fi; in a chain, the strongest one is usually the closest. Joining one is for FireFly only, and Android asks you first.
No hotspots found. Android allows only a few scans every two minutes: try again shortly.
Scanning needs the Nearby devices permission (location on older Android). FireFly uses it only to list Wi-Fi networks.
Couldn\'t join %1$s (cancelled, out of range, or a wrong password).
%1$s is joined, but no Stump answers there.
On this Android version, join the hotspot in the system\'s Wi-Fi settings; FireFly then finds it under This Wi-Fi.
This hotspot has a password. It\'s used for this connection only.
Stumps on the same Wi-Fi as you (%1$s): FireFly asks the network who\'s a Stump, by name, whatever address the router gave it. A few seconds.
No other Stump on this network.
Bars from the signal of the last message heard from each Stump.
No Stump heard on the radio yet.
chat is off on this node
not sent (too fast): tap to send again
You\'ve posted a few times in a minute: the node asks you to wait a moment.
Your radio settings differ from this Stump\'s
It uses %1$s. With different settings, LoRa never hears it.
not delivered: tap to send again
No radio: nothing can be sent over LoRa
Connect an RNode (Network tab), or reach this Stump over its Wi-Fi.
This Stump is also reachable over Wi-Fi.
%1$s answers at %2$s, this Wi-Fi\'s gateway: that\'s the Stump you\'re next to.
This Wi-Fi\'s gateway (%1$s) isn\'t a Stump: it\'s your router. To find a Stump on this network, use Find Stumps.
not sent (the Stump didn\'t answer): tap to send again
not sent: only verified people write in this room. Tap \"Verify me\", then tap here to send again
Delete this conversation. They can still write to you.
Delete it, and drop their private messages on this Stump.
The conversation with %1$s on this Stump is deleted from this phone. They can still write to you, which starts a new one.

The conversation is deleted, and from now on private messages from %1$s on this Stump are dropped on this phone, without a notification. They aren\'t told, and the Stump still carries them: it has no block of its own. You can unblock them in this Stump\'s private messages.
Where a Stump sends your private messages while you\'re on its Wi-Fi too. Over Wi-Fi: in the app while it\'s connected there. Over LoRa: always by radio. You\'re listed once either way.
This Stump is in a rescue start after failed starts: no radio, chain or plugins for now. Chat over Wi-Fi works; it returns to normal by itself.
